title: Machine-learning screening guides thermochemical measurements of salt hydrates
summary: Composition-based machine-learning models screened salt-hydration reactions, after which researchers synthesized and measured selected candidates by differential scanning calorimetry. The article reports volumetric energy densities of 1.74 ± 0.02, 1.73 ± 0.02 and 1.70 ± 0.02 GJ/m³ for three rubidium Tutton salt hydrates. These compounds were already known; the result is AI-guided thermochemical characterization, not new compound synthesis or demonstrated heat-storage deployment. An earlier preprint contains the measurements, but the date of its first public version is unclear, so no claim is made about which came first.
